itinerary.labelHtml:
The Itinerary

Day by day

Swipe each carousel for photos. Every stop carries its cost, a 💰 money-saving tip, an ✨ splurge, picky-kid restaurants, backup / if-time ideas, blog links, and a map — tap “Open in Google Maps” to navigate. Each day also shows an estimated per-day cost — food + activities only (excludes lodging, flights, and the rental car).

days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work
days.note: Leave Thursday evening so Friday can be the arrival day without burning a full extra workday before the trip starts.

days.heading: Arrive Antalya and ease into Kaleici
days.note: Pick up the car only if the hotel parking plan is clear. Otherwise transfer into Kaleici and collect the car the next morning.

spots.name: Kaleici Old Harbor + Mermerli Beach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KaleiciIG · MermerliFlickr
spots.cost: Old town wandering and harbor viewpoints are free. Mermerli Beach is paid/private-style; budget $25-$60 family depending loungers/drinks.
spots.climate: June: Antalya often runs around 86 F day / 66 F night; sea is commonly 77-79 F. Start slow after the overnight flight and use the hotel pool if jet lag wins.
spots.saveHtml: Save Make arrival day free: old harbor, Hadrian's Gate, sunset viewpoint, and a simple pizzeria dinner.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Use Mermerli Beach or a Konyaalti beach club on the first full day if the family needs loungers, shade, showers, and easy snacks.
spots.restoHtml:
• Il Vicino Pizzeria — Kaleici wood-fired pizza, pasta, calzones and gelato; the easiest first-night plain-food win
  • Rokka — casual wraps, falafel, chicken, fries and simple plates near Kaleici
  • BigChefs Antalya — large Turkish/international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken, breakfast and dessert fallbacks
spots.altboxHtml:
• Konyaalti Beach ↩ — better if the family wants a wider public beach, mountain backdrop, and easier parking than Kaleici.
  • Antalya Museum ↗ — air-conditioned substitute with Perge sculptures when ruins are too hot.
  • Duden Waterfalls ↗ — shorter, easier drama day with cliffside water.

days.heading: Perge and Aspendos before the heat
days.note: This is the main history day. If it is brutally hot, choose Aspendos plus Antalya Museum rather than forcing two exposed ruins.

spots.name: Perge + Aspendos Roman Ruins
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · PergeIG · AspendosFlickr
spots.cost: Plan roughly $90-$140 family if doing both Perge and Aspendos with foreign-visitor pricing; guided day tours often run around $90+ per adult, so self-drive is the saver.
spots.climate: June: hot, exposed ruins. Go early, cap it at two major stops, and return to pool/sea by mid-afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive and choose either Perge or Aspendos if heat is high; do not pay for a full tour unless you want narration and zero driving.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Hire a licensed guide for a half day if the family will actually listen; otherwise spend on shade, drinks, and a better pool hotel.
spots.restoHtml:
• Il Vicino Pizzeria — Kaleici wood-fired pizza, pasta, calzones and gelato; the easiest first-night plain-food win
  • Rokka — casual wraps, falafel, chicken, fries and simple plates near Kaleici
  • BigChefs Antalya — large Turkish/international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken, breakfast and dessert fallbacks
spots.altboxHtml:

  • Duden Waterfalls ↗ — shorter, easier drama day with cliffside water.
  • Kursunlu Waterfall ↗ — shadier nature stop if the coast is too hot.

days.heading: Termessos or Konyaalti recovery day
days.note: Use the family's jet-lag and heat tolerance to decide. Termessos is memorable, but a pool-and-Konyaalti day may be smarter with kids.

spots.cost: Termessos itself is a low-cash-entry ruin, but the family cost is the rental car, fuel, snacks, and energy. Budget $30-$80 plus lunch.
spots.climate: June: cooler than the coast but still an uphill, rocky walk. Wear real shoes; skip it if jet lag or heat is ugly.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use this as a free/cheap nature-history morning, then finish at Konyaalti instead of stacking another paid attraction.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Swap to a guided Termessos/Karain/Duden day only if nobody wants to drive switchbacks.
spots.restoHtml:
• Il Vicino Pizzeria — Kaleici wood-fired pizza, pasta, calzones and gelato; the easiest first-night plain-food win

  • BigChefs Antalya — large Turkish/international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken, breakfast and dessert fallbacks

days.heading: Drive the coast to Kas or Kalkan
days.note: Keep this westbound drive simple. Do not stack Kekova today; protect that as its own full boat day.

spots.name: Myra/Demre Coast Stop
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · MyraIG · DemreFlickr
spots.cost: Treat Myra/Demre as an optional transfer-day stop. Budget $40-$120 family for parking, snacks, and any current Myra entry fees; skip it if the drive is running long or the heat is already high.
spots.climate: June: exposed and hot by midday. This works only as a short morning/lunch stop on the Antalya-to-Kas drive, not as a full ruins day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use Demre/Myra as a quick leg-stretcher and lunch stop rather than booking another guided ruins tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add St. Nicholas Church or a short Demre boat detour only if the transfer day is moving easily.
spots.restoHtml:
• SpaghettiCi — Italian/pizza in Kas; pasta and pizza are the picky-kid anchor
  • Cafe Corner — broad international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken and Turkish mains
  • Hold&Bite — fast-casual burgers/fries/sandwiches for post-beach low-effort meals
spots.altboxHtml:
• Finike harbor ↩ — simple coast stop on the way to Kas if ruins and church time are not landing.
  • Hidayet Bay ↗ — easy clear-water swim close to Kas when a boat day is too much.
  • Meis / Kastellorizo ferry ↗ — passport-dependent Greek island stamp if the family wants a different kind of day.

days.heading: Kaputas and Patara water day
days.note: Kaputas is the postcard stop, but it is small and exposed. Pair it with Patara or a pool reset rather than trying to sit there all day.

spots.name: Kaputas Beach + Patara Sand
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KaputasIG · PataraFlickr
spots.cost: Kaputas is low-cost/free-ish depending current municipal rules; recent reports show small entry or lounger/umbrella fees. Patara can run up to about EUR15 pp when bundled with ancient-site access. Budget $70-$180 family depending loungers and whether Patara ruins are included.
spots.climate: June: Kas sea averages around 24 C / 75 F. Kaputas can have waves; Patara is wider and windier but better for long sand walks.
spots.saveHtml: Save Arrive at Kaputas before 9:30, bring towels and snacks, and skip paid loungers if you only need a two-hour swim.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pay for Patara ancient city + beach if the family wants a sand-and-ruins day instead of another cove stop.
spots.restoHtml:
• SpaghettiCi — Italian/pizza in Kas; pasta and pizza are the picky-kid anchor
  • Cafe Corner — broad international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken and Turkish mains
  • Hold&Bite — fast-casual burgers/fries/sandwiches for post-beach low-effort meals
spots.altboxHtml:
• Limanagzi Bay ↩ — car-free bay reached by short water taxi from Kas, calmer than Kaputas when road parking is ugly.
  • Meis / Kastellorizo ferry ↗ — passport-dependent Greek island stamp if the family wants a different kind of day.
  • Kalkan harbor ↗ — more polished dinner scene if Kas feels too low-key.

days.heading: Kekova Sunken City boat day
days.note: This is the signature Kas splurge candidate. Shared boat is budget-rational; private boat is the comfort play if this trip wins.

spots.name: Kekova Sunken City Boat Day
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KekovaFlickr
spots.cost: Shared Kas/Kekova boat trips commonly start around EUR40 pp; private boats can run EUR630-900+. For this family, plan $180-$330 shared or $700-$1,000 private.
spots.climate: June: prime boat weather, but sun exposure is the risk. Bring hats, rash guards, and cash for drinks.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use a shared boat from Kas or Ucagiz rather than a private family boat unless this is the trip's signature splurge.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Private Kekova boat is the best high-end spend on this itinerary if you want shade, pacing control, and no loud-party boat.
spots.restoHtml:
• SpaghettiCi — Italian/pizza in Kas; pasta and pizza are the picky-kid anchor
  • Cafe Corner — broad international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken and Turkish mains
  • Hold&Bite — fast-casual burgers/fries/sandwiches for post-beach low-effort meals
spots.altboxHtml:
• Greek island Meis / Kastellorizo ferry ↩ — passport-dependent day trip if the family wants a Greek island stamp instead of a second Turkish boat day.
  • Limanagzi Bay ↗ — car-free bay reached by short water taxi when Kaputas parking is ugly.
  • Kalkan harbor ↗ — more polished dinner scene if Kas feels too low-key.

days.heading: Kas town, theater, and Limanagzi
days.note: After the boat day, keep the last Kas day local: harbor, theater, water taxi to Limanagzi, or just pool and dinner.

spots.name: Kas Harbor, Antiphellos Theater + Limanagzi
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KasIG · AntiphellosIG · LimanagziFlickr
spots.cost: Kas theater and harbor wandering are free. Limanagzi water taxis/beach clubs are pay-as-you-go; budget $60-$180 family for boat rides, loungers, drinks, and lunch.
spots.climate: June: hot afternoons, lovely evenings. Use the town after 5pm and make the middle of the day water or pool time.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free theater-at-sunset walk and supermarket picnic instead of another ticketed excursion.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a low-key Limanagzi or island-hopping lunch boat if everyone wants one more swim day without a long drive.
spots.restoHtml:
• SpaghettiCi — Italian/pizza in Kas; pasta and pizza are the picky-kid anchor
  • Cafe Corner — broad international menu with burgers, pasta, chicken and Turkish mains
  • Hold&Bite — fast-casual burgers/fries/sandwiches for post-beach low-effort meals
spots.altboxHtml:
• Kalkan harbor evening ↩ — more polished dinner scene if the family chooses Kalkan as the base instead of Kas.
  • Kalkan harbor ↗ — more polished dinner scene if Kas feels too low-key.
  • Patara ruins and beach ↗ — big sand plus history when the family wants variety in one stop.

days.heading: Observed Juneteenth transfer through Saklikent
days.note: Use the holiday as a transfer day. Saklikent gives the drive a purpose, but skip tubing if the canyon is crowded or the water shocks the 8-year-old.

spots.name: Saklikent Gorge + Tlos Transfer Day
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · SaklikentIG · TlosFlickr
spots.cost: 2026 local guides list Saklikent entry around 250 TL adults / 125 TL students; add shoe rental, parking, lunch platforms, or tubing. Budget $60-$180 family depending extras.
spots.climate: June: hot outside, icy snowmelt water inside the gorge. Wear old sneakers/water shoes and expect wet legs.
spots.saveHtml: Save Bring old shoes and dry clothes; shoe rentals and impulse snacks add up.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add tubing/rafting only if the 8-year-old is confident in cold, moving water.
spots.restoHtml:
• Bella Gusto — Oludeniz menu includes burgers, chicken burgers, pizza/pasta-style comfort food and desserts
  • Pizza Pepino — Hisaronu/Ovacik Italian and steakhouse option with delivery-friendly pizza/pasta
  • Mozaik Bahce — Fethiye town Turkish comfort food; use pide/kofte/chicken basics for cautious eaters
spots.altboxHtml:
• Kayakoy Ghost Village ↩ — shorter, drier history stop if the gorge sounds too physical on transfer day.
  • Kidrak Beach ↗ — quieter paid beach near Blue Lagoon when crowds are annoying.
  • Calis Beach sunset ↗ — easy promenade, sunset, and dinner when the family wants low effort.

days.heading: Oludeniz Blue Lagoon and Kayakoy
days.note: Do the lagoon early, retreat for pool time, then visit Kayakoy late afternoon when the stone village is less punishing.

spots.name: Oludeniz Blue Lagoon + Kayakoy
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · OludenizIG · Blue LagoonIG · KayakoyFlickr
spots.cost: Blue Lagoon walk-in entry is commonly reported around 100-150 TL pp in 2026, with parking around 500-600 TL and lounger sets extra. Kayakoy is about EUR3 pp. Budget $60-$180 family.
spots.climate: June: warm air, comfortable sea, and intense sun. Go early or late; the lagoon gets crowded fast.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use free Belcekiz public beach first, then pay for the lagoon only if the family wants calmer water and shade.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Paragliding from Babadag is the famous Oludeniz splurge, but only for willing older kid/adults and only with a very reputable operator.
spots.restoHtml:
• Bella Gusto — Oludeniz menu includes burgers, chicken burgers, pizza/pasta-style comfort food and desserts
  • Pizza Pepino — Hisaronu/Ovacik Italian and steakhouse option with delivery-friendly pizza/pasta
  • Mozaik Bahce — Fethiye town Turkish comfort food; use pide/kofte/chicken basics for cautious eaters
spots.altboxHtml:

  • Calis Beach sunset ↗ — easy promenade, sunset, and dinner when the family wants low effort.
  • Katranci Bay Nature Park ↗ — pine-backed beach picnic if another boat day is too much.

days.note: Choose the route based on family mood: 12 Islands for calmer swimming and value; Butterfly Valley for cliffs and drama.

spots.climate: June: excellent swim weather. The issue is sun and boat style, not water temperature.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose the 12 Islands tour from Fethiye harbor for calmer family swimming and lower cost.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Choose a smaller no-loud-music Butterfly Valley boat or private speedboat if scenery beats price.

  • Gemiler Beach ↗ — quiet beach near Kayakoy when Oludeniz is too busy.

days.heading: Dalyan/Iztuzu or Fethiye flex day
days.note: This is deliberately flexible. Dalyan adds river tombs and turtle beach; a down day protects the trip if everyone is over boats and drives.

spots.name: Dalyan River + Iztuzu Turtle Beach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · DalyanIG · IztuzuFlickr
spots.cost: Iztuzu beach itself is often free or symbolic-entry, with loungers/umbrellas extra; classic Dalyan river cruises with rock tombs, mud baths, and Iztuzu commonly run about $35-$50 pp from Dalyan. Budget $140-$420 family depending self-drive versus tour.
spots.climate: June: hot, sunny, and exposed on the river and beach. It is best as a morning-to-midafternoon day with hats, water, and a willingness to skip mud baths if the family is done.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive to Dalyan or Iztuzu and use the beach plus tomb viewpoints instead of buying a full-day excursion.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a Dalyan riverboat with lunch and mud baths if the family wants a no-planning nature/history day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Bella Gusto — Oludeniz menu includes burgers, chicken burgers, pizza/pasta-style comfort food and desserts
  • Pizza Pepino — Hisaronu/Ovacik Italian and steakhouse option with delivery-friendly pizza/pasta
  • Mozaik Bahce — Fethiye town Turkish comfort food; use pide/kofte/chicken basics for cautious eaters
spots.altboxHtml:
• Fethiye pool and harbor day ↩ — the lower-effort choice if two straight water/boat days have already been enough.
  • Dalyan and Iztuzu Turtle Beach ↗ — river, rock tombs, turtles, and sand if you want variety over another sea boat.
  • Gemiler Beach ↗ — quiet beach near Kayakoy when Oludeniz is too busy.

days.heading: Final beach, market, and packing day
days.note: Do not make the last full day a long excursion. Use it for the missed favorite: lagoon, Calis, Fethiye old town, or hotel pool.

spots.climate: June: hot, bright, and easy for one last swim. Avoid a long excursion so packing and the Dalaman departure stay calm.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the hotel pool, Fethiye harbor, or a free beach stretch instead of another paid boat or beach club.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do one sunset drink/dessert stop or a nicer final dinner if the flight-day packing is already handled.

days.heading: Fly Dalaman to Pittsburgh
days.note: Return from Dalaman, not Antalya. Build a generous airport buffer because international summer check-in lines can be slow.

Strong fit

Best remaining warm-water Europe-style answer

June sea temperatures are already comfortable on this coast: Antalya is commonly around 25-26 C / 77-79 F, and Kas is around 24 C / 75 F. That is a materially warmer water profile than Portugal, California, or early-June Atlantic options.

The airfare quote decides whether this is a finalist

Recent public fare signals put PIT-AYT around $900-$1,300 pp round-trip, while PIT-DLM/DLM-PIT can price higher. Treat $5.6k family airfare as the cap-fit gate; above that, the high end drifts over $15k.

Juneteenth saves a vacation day

Depart after work Thu Jun 10, arrive Antalya Fri Jun 11, use observed Juneteenth on Fri Jun 18 as the Fethiye transfer day, and fly home Wed Jun 23. That makes a 12-night trip about 8 PTO days.

Save money

  • Use AYT-in/DLM-out only if the premium is reasonable. If open-jaw adds more than ~$800 family, re-check round-trip Antalya and one-way transfer math.
  • Book apartments/aparthotels with pools. Turkey's lodging value is best when you avoid full-service resorts but still get AC, space, kitchen, and pool.
  • Make Kekova shared unless it is the signature splurge. Private boats are wonderful but can add $500-$800 over shared seats.
  • Skip daily beach clubs. Use public beaches, hotel pool resets, and paid loungers only on true all-day water days.
  • Self-drive ruins. Guided Perge/Aspendos/Termessos days multiply costs quickly for four people.
  • Use pide/kofte/pizza nights. Casual dinners are one of the best Turkey budget levers and still work for picky eaters.

Worth the splurge

  • Private Kekova boat. Best single comfort splurge if the family wants shade, quieter pacing, and swim-stop control.
  • Pool-forward Kas/Kalkan lodging. Worth paying for because the middle base carries the best water stretch.
  • Small Oludeniz boat. Choose a no-loud-music or smaller route if Butterfly Valley scenery matters.
  • One guided ruins morning. Use a guide only where story matters most, probably Perge/Aspendos, not every site.
  • Paragliding. Iconic in Oludeniz, but optional and age/nerve/operator-dependent.

The stuff nobody tells you

Operational notes researched July 2026; confirm official flight, museum, beach, road, and operator details before paying.

Book in roughly this order

  1. Flights · as soon as June 2027 fares are useful
  2. Family lodging with parking/pool · immediately after flights
  3. Rental car · after lodging parking is confirmed

  5. Fethiye/Oludeniz boat · 4-8 weeks out

Documents

US family basics

  • No Turkey e-Visa for ordinary US passports. Turkey's MFA lists ordinary US passport holders as visa-exempt up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
  • Passports still matter. Use the usual six-month-validity comfort rule even when formal visa friction is low.
  • Carry license + IDP. Turkey car rentals may ask for an International Driving Permit alongside the US license.

Flights

Avoid routing traps

  • Dalaman exit is the point. Do not backtrack to Antalya unless airfare savings clearly beat the time cost.
  • Istanbul connection. If Turkish Airlines prices well, IST gives easy onward hops to Antalya and Dalaman; still leave real connection padding.
  • Seat assignments. Pay early to keep the four seats together on long-haul legs.

Driving

Turquoise Coast rhythm

  • Daylight only. The D400 is beautiful but curvy; transfer days should finish before dark.
  • Parking in old towns. Kaleici and Kas are not where you improvise parking with luggage. Confirm details before booking.
  • Fuel and snacks. Top up before long coast drives and carry water; the prettiest stretches are not the easiest service stops.

Water Days

Make the heat work for you

  • Beach mornings. Kaputas, Blue Lagoon, and Patara are better before peak parking and sun.
  • Rash guards. Useful on boat days where shade is limited and sunscreen reapplication gets old.
  • Saklikent shoes. Bring old sneakers or rent grip shoes; flip-flops are a bad idea in the gorge.

Food

Picky-eater plan

  • Pide is your friend. It reads like Turkish pizza and is widely available.
  • Use big-menu restaurants strategically. Bella Gusto, BigChefs-style places, and Kas Italian spots are there for tired nights.
  • Breakfasts are easy. Turkish hotel breakfasts, bakeries, simit, fruit, yogurt, and eggs reduce morning friction.
